question.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14268503/assets/55d5d5dc4af3eaf8d0bf0474fd77731242346be452c109d6bbc6fdb52033a647.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14268503/assets/6dc2b50d6bb8a7d2fcc50be918737857d065088320010a356c626e1417efcc82.svg) are orthogonal vectors, find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =5\cdot (-4)+(-3)\cdot 6+k\cdot (-6)+(-2)\cdot 8 \\  & =-20-18-6k-16 \\  & =-6k-54.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the last line to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-6k-54 & =0 \\ -6k & =54 \\ k & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$
